html:
Cheyenne-Arapaho (Oklahoma) marks the land of the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes in western Oklahoma, with their offices at Concho. These are the Southern Cheyenne and Southern Arapaho, two Algonquian-speaking Plains peoples who were allies.

Both had moved onto the Plains and lived by hunting bison on horseback. In 1864 Colorado militia killed peaceful Cheyenne and Arapaho at Sand Creek. The Medicine Lodge Treaty of 1867 assigned them a reservation in Indian Territory, and in 1868 Custer's troops attacked Black Kettle's camp on the Washita River there. In 1892 their reservation was split into allotments and the rest was opened to white settlers in a land run.
